newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS - Spreads wane amid supply boon.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS - Spreads wane amid supply boon.

text.p: Heavy supply of global and Yankee bond issues combined with moderate selling in the 10-year sector of the curve on Wednesday to push spreads marginally wider, traders said.
High-yields, meanwhile, saw sluggish trade with some new issues quoted down as much as one point, dealers said.

More than $2.5 billion in high-grade supply was seen providing best value for buyers, traders said, leaving secondary spreads wider by one to two basis points. Further, the recent flattening in the five to 10-year segment of the curve placed broad pressure on 10-year paper, they said.

Leading supply was a $1.0 billion 10-year AAA-rated bond issue from Bayerische Landesbank's New York branch, priced via Merrill Lynch & Co Inc and J.P. Morgan to yield 25 basis points over Treasuries.
Also on Wednesday, American Express Co issued $500 million A1/A-plus-rated seven-year global debt, priced to yield 39 basis points off the curve via Lehman Brothers.
Some traders opined the AMEX deal was the most aggressively priced of the bunch, but most reported solid orders for the new high-grade deals.

Moving on, the Republic of South Africa issued $500 million in 20-year Baa3/BB-plus rated Yankee debt to yield 183 basis points over Treasuries; Salomon Inc issued $400 million in three-year Baa1/BBB-rated debt to yield 58 basis points over; and Toro Corp issued $175 million of Baa3/BBB-minus rated two-tranche debt to yield 80 basis points over for 10-year paper and 113 basis points over for 30-years.
Still to come include Yankees from the Philippines, Mexico and Russia, market sources said.
In the high-yield arena, prices were under pressure as some fund managers staged "a little buyers strike," as put by Prudential Investments' portfolio manager George Edwards.

"New issues are just being ripped out of the woodwork and are being marketed with same-day type of service, no roadshows, they are low single-Bs at 225 over and my reaction is the market is just backing off that stuff," Edwards said.
Edwards said managers have the luxury to be more selective in dealing with a large but not overwhelming calendar of issues. Cash flows remain at adequate levels, he said.
Some high-yield deals priced recently have traded off as much as one point, with the broadcasting credits taking the brunt of the pressure, traders said.

Tuesday's $200 million Young Broadcasting 10-year senior subordinated notes were quoted in a 98 bid, 98-1/2 offer market on Wednesday compared with an original level of 99.08. And Jacor Communications' $150 million 10-year senior subordinated notes, priced last week, were also quoted one point lower than its initial level.

One exception was Chancellor Broadcasting's $200 million 10-year senior subordinated notes, said one trader. The notes were seen in a 99 bid, 99-3/4 offer market compared with Wednesday's issued level of 98.887.
Issuance, as a result, slowed on Wednesday, dealers said.

One quick marketing included Horseshoe Gaming LLC's $165 million 10-year B3/single-B rated senior subordinated notes, priced as 9-3/8s to yield 300 basis points over Treasuries via Wasserstein Perrella (Grantchester Securities,) according to a high-yield trading source.
The issue was increased in size by $20 million. It priced at the wide end of price talk.
